newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government wins milk confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy government wins milk confidence vote.

text.p: ROME, March 26 (REuter) - The government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday won a confidence vote in the Senate to ram through a bill to reform the milk sector.
As expected, the government won the vote in the Senate (upper house), where it has a clear majority. It won a similar vote in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) last week.
The centre-left government won the Senate vote with a count of 156 for and 76 against.
The decree bill relates to a package of reforms for the dairy sector, which has been hit by a bitter dispute with farmers over strict European Union quotas.
The decree contains emergency aid measures and was introduced by the government in January after farmers blockaded roads and airports to protest against EU overproduction fines.
The farmers had accused the government of failing to advise them of their correct quotas and initially refused to pay.
The bill approved on Wednesday offers cheap loans, payments of fines by installment and a pledge to set up a commission to examine grievances.

The European Commission decided earlier this month to withhold farm funds due to Italy, Spain and Greece for failing to pay the so-called EU super-levy fines for overshooting their strict 1995-96 milk output quotas.
Italian farmers were fined 192.2 million Ecus ($167 million).
Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas.
